rationale: C18 is the proclamation that the child expressly supplements and amends. The child reuses C18's specialized trade-agreement machinery, including its statutory authority, Cuban preferential-tariff framework, recital-and-list structure, operative application rules, and exception for more favorable customs treatment. It then adds items to C18's lists, deletes and corrects specific entries, and preserves the relationship between the general agreement and Cuba's exclusive agreement. This is concrete, material drafting dependence, not merely a shared trade topic. C04 and C13 involve amendment or delegation machinery but lack comparable substantive or linguistic correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the addition of the following items to the list set forth in the 8th recital of said proclamation of January 1, 1948 ... is required or appropriate to carry out said exclusive trade agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the rates of duty and import tax specified in the column at the right of the respective descriptions of products listed in the 8th and 9th recitals of this proclamation shall be applied
shared_material.explanation: The child directly modifies the tariff lists established by C18.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the rates of duty specified in the column at the right of the respective descriptions of products ... shall be applied subject to the applicable terms, conditions, and qualifications ... to products of the republic of Cuba
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The rates of duty and import tax specified in the column at the right of the respective descriptions of products ... shall be applied, subject to the applicable terms, conditions, and qualifications ... to the products of the Republic of Cuba
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reuses C18's distinctive operative formula for applying listed Cuban tariff rates.

shared_material.child_excerpt: no such rate shall be applied to a particular article ... if, when the article is entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption, more favorable customs treatment is prescribed for the article by a statute, proclamation, or Executive order then in effect
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The provisions of subdivisions (a), (b), and (c) shall not apply to a particular article ... if, when the articles is entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption, more favorable customs treatment is prescribed therefore by a statute, proclamation, or executive order then in effect
shared_material.explanation: This is a near-literal reuse of C18's specialized savings clause.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the first item 506 and item 752 shall be deleted ... the figure and word "4/5 of" shall be deleted ... item 1527(a)(2) ... shall be changed
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the respective descriptions of products listed in the 8th and 9th recitals of this proclamation
shared_material.explanation: The child's operative provisions amend particular entries in C18, making C18 the indispensable structural basis for the later drafting.
